title: SDK Onramp Signal Framework — enterprise streaming ergonomics & auth prioritization
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Background: We receive recurring enterprise requests for better SDK onboarding patterns covering language bindings, auth token refresh/rotation, resumable streaming ergonomics, and checklist signals for sales/onboarding. This ticket scopes a signal framework to intake and prioritize SDK and client library requests in a way that surfaces enterprise constraints (SAML/KMS, VPC, compliance) and developer ergonomics (stream resume, backpressure, reconnect). The deliverable is a triage rubric, onboarding checklist, and prototype priority UI for the Console's SDK intake flow.

Problem statement: Sales & SEs keep sending ad-hoc SDK asks; engineering feedback shows many duplicates across languages and similar auth patterns. We need a repeatable triage process to route work to bindings, runtime, or docs and to quantify expected engineering effort and compliance risk.

Goals:
- Define signals to score SDK requests (customer size, security needs, streaming model, retry semantics, latency constraints, bindings maturity).
- Produce a triage rubric and checklist that maps requests to outcomes: quick-doc-ship, design spike, binding-implementation, or product bet.
- Prototype a Console intake page wireframe + backend metadata fields to capture those signals.
- Pilot the rubric on 20 incoming requests and measure routing accuracy vs. engineering outcome.

Out of scope: Implementation of every language binding; this ticket focuses on intake, scoring, and routing rules.
acceptance_criteria: Documented rubric with 7 signals and scoring thresholds published to Confluence
Prototype Console intake form mock (Figma link) reviewed by UX and SE
Mapping table from scores to outcomes (Docs/Spike/Implement) with estimated T-shirt effort
Pilot completed on 20 requests with annotated outcomes and a short retrospective
notes: Signal candidates: customer_security_profile, streaming_latency_sensitivity, required_auth_pattern (oauth/jwt/saml), resumable_stream_required, language_priority, existing_integration_complexity, compliance_impact
Trade-offs: capturing more signals increases intake friction; aim for 6-8 high-signal fields.
Suggested scoring: weight security and streaming ergonomics higher for enterprise customers.
Engineering concerns: need telemetry to verify streaming resume behavior across bindings; runtime might require minor SDK hooks to surface reconnect tokens.
Related artifacts: initial qualitative interview notes with 6 SEs and 3 Sales ENGs available in Confluence.
